To catalyze a paradigm shift towards a resilient, low-carbon, nature-positive and socially inclusive urban development in Grand Libreville through an integrated urban land planning fostered by a multi-scale, multi-actor and multi-sectoral governance system

Yes Normal 0 false false false EN-US JA AR-SA /* Style Definitions */ table.MsoNormalTable {mso-style-name:"Table Normal"; mso-tstyle-rowband-size:0; mso-tstyle-colband-size:0; mso-style-noshow:yes; mso-style-priority:99; mso-style-parent:""; mso-padding-alt:0in 5.4pt 0in 5.4pt; mso-para-margin-top:0in; mso-para-margin-right:0in; mso-para-margin-bottom:8.0pt; mso-para-margin-left:0in; line-height:107%; mso-pagination:widow-orphan; font-size:11.0pt; font-family:"Calibri",sans-serif; mso-ascii-font-family:Calibri; mso-ascii-theme-font:minor-latin; mso-hansi-font-family:Calibri; mso-hansi-theme-font:minor-latin; mso-bidi-font-family:Arial; mso-bidi-theme-font:minor-bidi;} The “Integrated governance and urban transformation for a sustainable Grand Libreville” project will contribute to four of the expected Global Environmental Benefits of the GEF-8 programming architecture: (i) climate change mitigation and adaptation, (ii) biodiversity conservation, (iii) reduced land degradation, and (iv) reduction of chemicals and waste. This project is aligned with the GEF-8 strategy of the Sustainable Cities Integrated Program and will contribute to developing innovative sustainability solutions and strengthening institutional capacity to transition towards building net zero carbon, nature positive, inclusive and climate resilient cities. The project will do so by implementing all of the program’s key strategic entry points: · Advancing integrated and systems-based interventions: this project will adopt an integrated approach for systemic transformation through (i) spatial integration and planning by working to strengthen the regulatory framework (Component 1) and planning with respect to mobility (Component 3) and urban green infrastructures (Component 2); and (ii) institutional integration by focusing on improving vertical and horizontal coordination (Component 1). · Integrating nature in urban development and regional planning: this project will advance the integration of nature into Grand Libreville by focusing on planning and pilot interventions with a view to increasing inclusive access to urban green infrastructures and the ecosystem services they generate for all (Component 2). · Decarbonizing the built environment: the SCIP Gabon project will support the strengthening of the regulatory framework surrounding the built environment to better integrate environmental considerations in urban planning and building practices (Component 1), will demonstrate the feasibility of best practices in eco-construction (Component 3) and will propose innovative financing mechanisms to upscale sustainable built environment (Component 1). It will also contribute to decarbonize urban mobility, by promoting active mobility and penalizing high polluting vehicles (output 2.1.2), and waste management, by fostering valorization of organic and non-organic waste (output 2.1.3). · Adopting circular economy approaches: this project will promote circularity in the construction and energy sectors through the recycling of locally produced wood, metal, plastic and organic waste (Component 3). · Promoting innovating financing: this SCIP Gabon project will support Gabon in general, and Grand Libreville specifically, in developing economic incentives to stimulate funding for green investments (Component 1). In addition, the project will bring significant socio-economic benefits. In particular, 750,000 people (367,500 women and 382,500 men) should benefit from the project, corresponding to 75% of Grand Libreville’s inhabitants. They will benefit from the increased and sustained provision of ecosystem services, which will be promoted through the implementation of ecosystem conservation and restoration and afforestation activities included in component 2. In this sense, the project will contribute to the regulation of the climate and to flood and erosion control, increasing the resilience to climate change of local communities. Given local temperatures and the urban heat island effect, the cooling effect of greenery will be particularly beneficial, especially for elderly, children and people with a preexisting negative health condition and stress. Furthermore, the project will preserve the cultural services provided by local ecosystems, including sacred forests, which are essential to local populations, and the four protected areas, which are visited by local residents. By ensuring green infrastructure is conserved and enhanced in the city, and not only in the outskirts, the project will contribute to a more equitable access to quality green spaces, which are currently more accessible for those with private vehicles allowing them to visit the protected areas in the outskirts of the city. Furthermore, by supporting the development of a low-emissions mobility system, and monitoring air quality, and disseminating air pollution warnings, output 3.1.1 should contribute to a reduction in the incidence of respiratory diseases. Moreover, by promoting active mobility, the project will improve the health of local residents, as well as the safety of those already walking. Output 3.1.2 will contribute to improving the residential comfort and generate savings through the promotion of eco-construction techniques and materials, including energy efficiency, achieving better energy outcomes with less expenses. Outcomes 3.1 will contribute to boosting the local economy, promoting green growth in the buildings, infrastructure, waste management and urban and peri-urban agriculture sectors. Indeed, outputs 3.1.1 to 3.1.3 will help strengthen several value chains and increase revenues of stakeholders by creating a market for eco-buildings and infrastructures and waste products especially organic waste such as woody and non-woody biomass, plastic and metallic waste. Improvements in waste management will reduce the pollution of ecosystems, enhancing human health. Through outputs 2.1.2 and 3.1.3, the project will contribute to reduced flood reduction (increased permeability, reduced blockage of sewage), thus reducing loss and damage related to flooding, and their negative physical, psychological and financial impact. In addition, in the longer-run, results from Output 1.2.1 should serve to increase the national budget (through new revenue streams and less reconstruction and rehabilitation expenses) and boost public and private investments toward sustainability goals. The SCIP Gabon project will also integrate gender and social inclusion considerations, including people with limited mobility, transversally throughout the project Alignment with multilateral agreements The “Integrated governance and urban transformation for a sustainable Grand Libreville” project is aligned with the main multilateral agreements: 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development: the project will directly support Gabon’s progress towards the following Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): - Goal 3: Good health and well-being. The project will contribute to target 3.9 of significantly reducing the number of deaths and illnesses from hazardous chemicals and air, water and soil pollution and contamination. - Goal 7: Affordable and clean energy. In particular, the project will contribute towards targets 7.2 and 7.3. respectively related to renewable energy and energy efficiency. - Goal 9: Industry, innovation and infrastructure. The SCIP Gabon project particularly will contribute to target 9.4 of upgrading infrastructure to make them sustainable, with increased resource-use efficiency and greater adoption of clean and environmentally sound technologies and industrial processes. - Goal 11: Sustainable cities and communities. Above all, the SCIP Gabon project will contribute to SDG 11 to make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable. In particular, the project will notably support targets 11.2, “by 2030, provide access to safe, affordable, accessible and sustainable transport systems for all, improving road safety, notably by expanding public transport, with special attention to the needs of those in vulnerable situations, women, children, persons with disabilities and older persons”; 11.3, “by 2030, enhance inclusive and sustainable urbanization and capacity for participatory, integrated and sustainable human settlement planning and management in all countries”; 11.6, “by 2030, reduce the adverse per capita environmental impact of cities, including by paying special attention to air quality and municipal and other waste management”; and 11.7, “by 2030, provide universal access to safe, inclusive and accessible, green and public spaces, in particular for women and children, older persons and persons with disabilities”. - Goal 12: Responsible consumption and production. The project will support the attainment of target 12.5 regarding the reduction of waste generation through prevention, reduction, recycling and reuse. - Goal 13: Climate action. The project will contribute to the achievement of target 13.2 on the integration of climate change measures into national policies, strategies and planning, as well as target 13.3 on the development of human and institutional capacity on climate change mitigation and adaptation. - Goal 15: Life on land. The SCIP project will support the achievement of target 15.9 on the integration of ecosystem and biodiversity values into national and local planning and development processes, and 15.2 regarding the sustainable management of forests and the substantial increase in afforestation and reforestation efforts. Convention on Biological Diversity/New Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework: The project will contribute to several Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) targets including Target 1, “plan and manage all areas to reduce biodiversity loss”; Target 2, “restore 30% of all degraded ecosystems”; Target 3, “conserve 30% of land, waters and seas”; Target 7, “reduce pollution to levels that are not harmful to biodiversity”; Target 8, “Minimize the Impacts of Climate Change on Biodiversity and Build Resilience”; Target 11, “restore, maintain and enhance nature’s contributions to people”; Target 12, “enhance green spaces and urban planning for human well-being and biodiversity”, Target 14, “integrate biodiversity in decision-making at every level; Target 18, “reduce harmful incentives by at least USD500 billion per year, and scale up positive incentives for biodiversity”; Target 19 on resource mobilization for biodiversity; and Target 20 on capacity building. United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change: The SCIP Gabon project is consistent with the Convention, and in particular with Article 4 paragraph 1d, “Promote sustainable management, and promote and cooperate in the conservation and enhancement, as appropriate, of sinks and reservoirs of all greenhouse gases not controlled by the Montreal Protocol, including biomass, forests and oceans, as well as, other terrestrial, coastal and marine ecosystems”; (f), “Take climate change considerations into account, to the extent feasible, in their relevant social, economic and environmental policies and actions, and employ appropriate methods, for example impact assessments, formulated and determined nationally, with a view to minimizing adverse effects on the economy, on public health and on the quality of the environment, of projects or measures undertaken by them to mitigate or adapt to climate change”; and (i), “Promote and cooperate in education, training and public awareness related to climate change and encourage the widest participation in this process, including that of non-governmental organizations”. Paris Agreement: this project is aligned with the Paris Agreement, signed by Gabon in 2016, through Article 5 paragraph 1, “Parties should take action to conserve and enhance, as appropriate, sinks and reservoirs of greenhouse gases as referred to in Article 4, paragraph 1 (d), of the Convention, including forests”. It is also coherent with Article 7 paragraph 1 which states that “Parties hereby establish the global goal on adaptation of enhancing adaptive capacity, strengthening resilience and reducing vulnerability to climate change, with a view to contributing to sustainable development and ensuring an adequate adaptation response”. Alignment with regional policies and instruments The SCIP Gabon project is aligned with the Central African Forest Commission (COMIFAC) regional policies on forest conservation and sustainable management, promoting biodiversity and environmental protection in the Congo Basin. It is also aligned with the Economic Community of Central African States (ECCAS) Environmental Policy by addressing sustainable urban development and environmental conservation thereby contributing to ECCAS’s objective to promote environmental sustainability and natural resource management in the Central African region. Finally, by adopting a comprehensive approach to sustainable urban transformation, SCIP Gabon aligns with the African Union’s Agenda 2063 which envisions inclusive growth, sustainable development and improved quality of life for African citizens. Alignment with national policies and instruments National Transition Development Plan (PNDT 2024-2026): This SCIP Gabon project is aligned with the National Transition Development Plan, which is the national development framework aimed at “restoring state institutions, consolidating inclusive and sustainable economic growth supported by more effective national governance by focusing on human capital development and infrastructure.” In particular, the project supports the fifth objective, namely sustainable and economic development, and the fourth pillar of the strategy aimed at strengthening environmental sustainability and resilience to climate change. In this context, the overall objective is to diversify the economy and support inclusive social development while promoting sustainable natural resource management, remaining a carbon-neutral country, and improving the disaster risk management and prevention framework. The project is fully in line with this objective as it contributes to Gabon's biodiversity and ecosystem protection goals by ensuring that urban expansion does not compromise natural areas and that urban areas are equipped with green infrastructure. It also aims to contribute to the development of a low-emission mobility system, improve the sustainability of the built environment, and promote new economic sectors based on the green economy and waste management in order to reduce pollution. It should be noted that with the election of Brice Clotaire OLIGUI NGUEMA as President of the Gabonese Republic on April 12, 2025, it is expected that Gabon's development plan beyond 2026 will continue along the lines set out during the political transition period and the PNDT. National Climate Plan (PNC) (2012) : this project is consistent with the PNC on the following: (i) the SCIP project will support sectoral GHG emissions reduction in the forestry, energy, construction and waste sectors; (ii) the project will contribute to enhancing resilience to climate change impacts via improved access to urban green infrastructures; (iii) the project will implement activities to strengthen the institutional and regulatory frameworks for climate action; (iv) the SCIP project will contribute to identifying and mobilizing funding sources for climate initiatives. Sustainable Development Orientation Law (N°002/2014 of August 2014): the SCIP Gabon project is fully coherent with the Sustainable Development Orientation Law, which establishes the foundational principles and strategic directions for sustainable development in Gabon. Indeed, the project contributes to reinforcing the rule of law by establishing clear frameworks for sustainable urban management; its aims at improving quality of life for all Grand Libreville’s inhabitants through greening investments, management of green spaces and through the promotion of low-carbon mobility; it seeks to integrated gender and social inclusivity considerations into urban planning; and finally, the project will contribute to the law’s emphasis on the development of financial tools to support sustainable development projects. 2nd Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC, 2020-2025): the NDC provides data on emissions per sector from 2005 placing the forestry and other land uses sector (FAT) as the most emitting sector (35,623 GgCO2eq in gross emissions), followed by energy (3,338 GgCO2eq) and agriculture (799 GgCO2eq). Through this document, Gabon committed to remain carbon neutral and to strive to maintain its annual net carbon absorption at 100 million TCO2eq to be achieved through sector specific reduction targets for 2030, including a 14.7% reduction in the forestry sector, 0.5% in the energy sector and 40.4% in the agriculture sector. The SCIP Gabon project contributes to these objectives via: - Activities to promote sustainable land use and compact urban development, supporting emissions reduction in the forestry and energy sectors. - Activities to promote energy efficiency and renewable energy use thereby reducing emissions in the energy sector. - The enhanced conservation of existing and creation of new green spaces that contribute to carbon sequestration, thereby supporting Gabon’s forestry sector emission reduction targets. - Activities aimed at limiting transport-, construction- and waste- related emissions contribute to the overall national reduction targets. - The improved management of organic waste and the production of compost support the emissions reduction target of the agriculture sector. It should be noted that, given the rapid urban growth in Gabon, particularly in GLBV, Gabon must strengthen the sustainability of its urban model in order to remain carbon neutral and prevent these urban centers from becoming hubs of increasing greenhouse gas emissions that could destabilize Gabon's carbon balance. National Energy Efficiency Strategy (2024): the SCIP Gabon project is aligned with the recently adopted National Energy Efficiency Strategy which seeks to promote energy efficiency in several sectors including the construction sector. The project will contribute to the objectives of this strategy by demonstrating a proof-of-concept through the rehabilitation of a public building, by introducing energy efficiency concepts in a new building code and by working on economic incentives to stir economic actors towards energy efficiency. The project is also consistent with several Gabonese legislations, including Law n°007/2014 on environmental protection, Law n°003/2007 on National Parks, the Forestry Code (Law n°016/01), Law n°037/2018 on mining regulations, Ordonnance n°019/2021 on climate change, Law n°0012/PR/2024 on plastic pollution, and Decree n°000541/PR/MEFEPEPN on waste elimination.
